answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a public key generated inside an attested enclave and to its measured code identity: MRENCLAVE for Intel SGX, with an equivalent launch measurement for AMD SEV. Remote verifiers accept signatures only after validating the hardware-backed attestation, so duplicating a virtual machine cannot clone the identity. An attacker must obtain additional physical silicon, not merely retell a fable of effortless nectar-fueled voyage.
